runtime-evidence:<path>.meaning: A recorded, labelled runtime run at <path> (repository-relative JSON object).
runtime-evidence:<path>.passes_when: the record has a top-level boolean outcome field (passed/ok/complete) equal to true, no non-empty failures or issues list, at least one recorded source identity matches the current tree, and every (path, sha256) pair recorded under source_sha256/source_identity/sources keys for an existing current file still equals that file. runtime-evidence:<path>.note: A record without an outcome field is a check failure, not evidence. Records whose hashes live under other keys (for example source_hashes, source_before/source_after) are not hash-bound by the verifier; where that is the case the route notes it.

premises: The effective request is an exact OutputRequest with an exact SecurityLabels value; confidentiality and clearance are exact native frozensets of inert strings. Annotations and constructors alone do not prove these premises (output_verification entry_premises).

Native dataclass/slot/classifier/frozenset semantics apply. Checked source definitions, annotation/type names, imported names, builtins and method bindings match runtime and remain unchanged; instance/class method shadowing is excluded by separate admission. Module/class initialization, assignment RHS evaluation, imports and constructors are not proved by this component and must separately establish these bindings.

The receiver is an exact ObjectManagerHost with native attribute access and no instance method shadowing. Its _lock is a native reentrant lock with no user callbacks and no exception suppression. Request fields and all relevant bindings remain stable across the call.
CPython semantics for exact type identity, native scalar/container operations, member/getset descriptors, generators and exception handling (output_data_verification _VALIDATOR_PREMISES).

Initialization and runtime binding: every derived module inventory holds the value of its source initializer, imported names select the named classes, and none is rebound afterwards (initialization_proved and runtime_binding_proved remain false).
Field stability: no other thread mutates the request, its labels or any traversed container during validation.

Process-global events are outside this model: cyclic garbage collection of unrelated objects (finalizers, weakref callbacks), signal handlers and asynchronous exceptions can run at allocation or bytecode boundaries.
Refusal tracebacks are not sanitized: literal refusal arguments carry no candidate data, but traceback frames reference the candidate, so callers must not publish them.

Remaining composition (output_verification): authorization of the effective request for its actual principal, destination and call context; admission of payload data/capabilities and label provenance; caller publication and pending-approval/continuation handling; every other request kind; complete placement and host isolation/lifetime.

All framework publication APIs (stream events, legacy event/log iterators, callbacks, current-state and history inspection) route through OutputMediator. This is enforced by the SGV109/SGV110 source-pattern regressions and the bounded before/after captures (raw/legacy-event-regression, raw/callback-regression, raw/state-publication-regression); the generic publication analysis still leaves 51/60 entries unresolved, so this is a regression-backed premise, not a proof.

admission.scope_note: Closed admission refuses any secured graph entry that is not an admitted execution descriptor before any compile-time candidate protocol runs in config.py. It closes the arbitrary node/branch body path within its admitted surface only. It does not prove imports, builder initialization, reducer/cache/retry callbacks, checkpointers, stream callbacks, module mutation, output publication, or compiler/decoder/OS enforcement, and it does not close SGV901 by itself. Routes R1-R4 consume it through the admission-surface check and the gate:admission:* checks; the verifier does not read this section directly.
